items_missed: No agenda statement and no 'sound good?' confirmation
Never asked whether they need packing services — this went completely unaddressed on a call where the customer said she'd move 'as many boxes as there is time for'
Never asked about storage stops or additional stops
Packing service pricing never quoted (follows from never probing packing)
Never asked walk distance / parking distance at either address
No size equivalents used (school bus reference)

Save Your Ass only partially landed — he said 'the more that you guys can accomplish before we even arrive the cheaper technically it will be', but gave no consolidation examples, no carload tip (customer volunteered the car idea herself for her plants), and no 'does that make sense' close
Never mentioned the bolded detail list at the top of the confirmation email
Never asked her to reply to the email with corrections
Used customer's name only once ('I got Allison Harley') — needs 3+
No 60¢/lb baseline mentioned alongside No Worries
Price readback was garbled in delivery — the customer had to restate the five-hour total back to him to confirm it was ~$1,000-$1,100 including the $75 travel fee
top_strength: Excellent recovery on a no-availability call — instead of losing the lead he worked three branches, found Leander, was upfront about the $75 travel fee and the cheaper hourly rate, then closed the booking on the call. He also caught that her self-reported 1,600 sqft was actually 1,180 and adjusted rather than quoting off a bad number.
coaching_note: Ask the packing question on every call — she said she'd take 'as many boxes as there is time for', which is the exact opening for a packing add-on and a Save Your Ass prep speech, and he took neither. Also read the final dollar range back cleanly instead of making the customer restate it.
phone_presence_notes: Natural, easy energy with real rapport moments (the cat joke, 'I respect that' on the tipping question) and an accommodating tone on the start-time change, but the customer's stream of 'mm-hmm's during the long pricing block shows he was monologuing more than checking in.
